result.title: SEEL: Towards End-to-End 3D Sign Generation with Language Models
result.summary: 3D sign language generation aims to produce signing motion from written text. Motivated by the linguistic nature of sign language, recent methods combine a motion tokenizer with a language model to predict motion tokens from text. However, both components are optimized through a two-stage pipeline with mismatched objectives: the tokenizer minimizes reconstruction error in isolation, while the generator learns from rigid one-hot reference tokens. A straightforward end-to-end extension bridges discrete token selection with straight-through estimators (STE), suffering from biased gradients and codebook collapse. To address these limitations, we propose SEEL, an end-to-end framework that aligns tokenization and generation with motion quality through two complementary mechanisms. First, to overcome rigid one-hot supervision, reconstruction-aware generation decodes candidate tokens in context and converts their 3D motion errors into soft targets, guiding the generator with physical motion quality. Second, to propagate generation feedback without STE, generation-aware tokenization passes continuous codebook expectations through the frozen generator, routing generated-motion gradients to the tokenizer to prevent codebook collapse. Combining both mechanisms enables the tokenizer and generator to co-evolve, achieving state-of-the-art performance on CSL-Daily, How2Sign, and Phoenix-2014T. Code and models will be released to facilitate future research.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SEEL，用「重建感知生成」把候选 motion token 的 3D 重建误差转成软目标，并用「生成感知分词」将连续 codebook 期望穿过冻结生成器回传梯度，实现 3D 手势生成的 tokenizer 与语言模型端到端协同训练，避免 STE 偏差与码本坍缩。
AI.relevance_reason: 离散视觉 token 的软目标监督与经冻结模型回传梯度，可能为 VLM 中 latent 视觉表示的训练监督与贡献分配提供线索，但该工作面向动作生成、无推理状态与证据使用环节，需核查可迁移性。
